accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA 8462 4.7.2.2–4.7.2.4: C=C is the alkene functional group and 'the generality of reactions of functional groups' determines organic reactions; alcohols carry –OH (methanol to butanol) and react with sodium; carboxylic acids carry –COOH (methanoic to butanoic acid), are weak acids, react with carbonates and with alcohols to give esters, ethyl ethanoate named. The lab's result table matches: only C=C clears bromine water, –OH and –COOH give hydrogen with sodium, only –COOH gives CO2 with carbonate, and the saturated ester gives none. Formula items (alcohol H = 2n+2, acid CnH2nO2, methyl ester H = 2n+2, ester carbons n+2) were checked at n = 1 and n = 5 by hand.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for this topic: treating the CH3 end or the whole molecule as the reactive part, circling only the O of –OH, circling only the OH of –COOH, calling ethanoic acid an alcohol because it contains O–H, confusing –COOH with –COO–, expecting a longer chain to change the reaction, expecting two-carbon compounds to react alike, and expecting the ester to keep fizzing because both reactants did.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is a reactivity bench built on this topic's own idea: the learner circles atoms of a displayed formula and gets checked against the true group; then runs three real diagnostic reagents on molecules where only the chain or only the group changes, filling a 4 x 3 results grid; then condenses ethanoic acid with ethanol by dragging and watches OH + H leave as water. flag_homo sorts series and plots boiling points, flag_alkene draws hydrogens and runs bromine only, flag_formula converts formula types; the 6-shingle gate is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Testing methanol to butanol with sodium gives the same fizz four times, so 'the chain comes along' is discovered; the two-carbon grid shows each group with its own unique column pattern, which is the definition of a functional group in action; the ester made in step 4 fails all three tests, showing the reactions belong to the group, not to the atoms that went in; the sorting step then turns the group into the family name.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions each with a tempting wrong option that the lab then disproves: 'the CH3 at the end' for ethanol's group, 'a longer chain changes the reaction' for butanol, 'both: same number of carbons' for ethane vs ethanol with sodium, 'yes: both starting chemicals fizzed' for the ester, and 'alcohols, because of the OH' for CH3COOH.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Walked in Chromium on desktop and iPhone 13: choosing –OH for propanoic acid is told the O–H sits on a C=O carbon and the four atoms act as –COOH; calling CH3COOCH3 a carboxylic acid is told the single-bonded O carries a carbon, not an H; picking –OH for a carbonate fizz is told alcohols fizz with sodium but not carbonate; 'no reaction: its chain is longer' for butanol is told the group decides; propanol for bromine water is told only C=C takes up bromine.

readability.evidence: Flesch-Kincaid grade 3.0 for the kid paragraphs and 6.7 for the adult paragraphs, within the 6.5 and 9.5 limits. The kid text moves from 'the chain is dull' to 'the group reacts' to the same-group rule with ethanol and butanol; the adult text gives one group per sentence with its test.

no_filler.evidence: Filler regex and the 12% explanation-overlap check pass, including against the homologous series and alkene lessons. Each adult paragraph has one job (definition and series consequence, the four groups with tests, ester formation, named mistakes); every lab message is built from the live molecule, reagent and result.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (390 px) for every step: molecules scale to the canvas width (butanol and ethyl ethanoate fit with end H atoms clear), the reagent shelf fits three across, bubbles are clipped to the tube, the 4 x 3 results grid is legible at 9.5 px headers, family bins wrap to two columns, and the atom buttons wrap without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA reports no violations in light and dark themes on desktop and phone; the canvas aria-label names the molecule, its condensed formula, the atoms in the chain, the circled atoms, the last test result and the full results grid; every atom has its own Circle button with a position label, and every drag (reagent onto molecule, acid onto alcohol) has a button.
